The present appeal is filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the MV Act') by the original claimant against judgment and award NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2999/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined dated 10.07.2024 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (hereinafter referred to as 'the tribunal') (Auxiliary), Mahisagar at Lunawada in Motor Accident Claim Petition (MACP) No.165 of 2023.

sentences.text: The parties will be referred as per their original position in the claim petition.

2. Short facts:
2.1
It is the case of the claimant that on 25.08.2023, the deceased Hiteshriben and Dharmishthaben were returning from Anand to Vadodara on Activa No.GJ-35 K-4280.
The deceased Hiteshriben was driving the Activa very slowly, with due care and caution, on the side of the road.

At about 17:30 hours, when they reached near the village Gohilpura on the Vasad - Vadodara highway, opponent No. 1 came driving a truck No.NL-01 Q-3269 in a rash and negligent manner, at an excessive speed, and lost control over the steering, violently dashing into the Activa from behind.
As a result, the deceased Hiteshriben sustained fatal injuries and ultimately succumbed to them.

Therefore, the claimant, who is the husband of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2999/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined deceased Hiteshriben, has filed the present claim petition seeking compensation of Rs. 1,20,00,000/- from the opponents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
2.2 The opponent Nos. 1 and 2 driver and owner of the truck have chosen not to appear.
Thereby, not contested claim petition.
Opponent No.3 have appeared and filed written statement.

So far as granting compensation to the claimant is concerned, after appreciating oral and documentary evidence on record, tribunal has awarded in all Rs.13,51,800/- after deducting 10% contributory negligence of deceased.
2.5 Being aggrieved and dissatisfied by the impugned award, present appeal is filed by the claimant challenging impugned judgment and award.

3. Submissions of appellant:
3.1

Learned advocate for the original claimant deceased was serving as Vocational trainer (teacher) in agricultural trade at D. N. High School, Anand and as per the documentary evidence submitted by claimant including bank account of deceased would clearly substantial the claim of claimants that deceased was used to earn Rs.15,000/- per month from his aforesaid employment.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2999/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined 3.2

He would submit that when there is a documentary evidence on record indicating monthly income of deceased of Rs.15000/- per months, tribunal has committed an error by considering only Rs.10,000/- per month income of the deceased.

3.3 He would further submit that as per the decision of Honourable Apex Court in case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors. reported in 2017 (13) Scale 12, Magma General Insurance Company Limited Versus Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram reported in 2018 (18)
SCC 130 and Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur Versus United India Insurance Co.Ltd. reported in AIR 2020 SC 3076 claimants would be entitled to received adequate amount of compensation which may be awarded by allowing present appeal.

4. Submissions of respondent:
4.1

Per contra Mr. H. G. Mazmudar, learned counsel for NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2999/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined opponent No.3 would submit that the tribunal has committed no error while granting compensation to the claimant.

He would submit that the deceased was used to receive Rs.15,000/-
per month as regular salary from his employment.
He has drawn attention of this Court to the observations made by the tribunal in para 10.1 of impugned judgment.
Thereby, would submit that income of deceased was variable which is much less then what is claimed by the claimant.
4.2 He would further submit that as per Exh. 39 which is so referred by the tribunal in para 4.1 of impugned judgment would indicate that deceased was serving on daily basis at the time of accident.
He would further submit that this Court may not accept arguments of claimants that income of deceased was Rs.15,000/- per month.
Although, he would fairly submit that income considered by the tribunal of Rs.10,000/- is contrary to documentary evidence.

He then left to the Court to decide an appropriate amount of income of Dhavalbhai Mahendrabhai Patel vs Pankajkumar Mannalal Varma on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148379742/

So,
he would request this Court to pass appropriate order in light of evidence on record.

5. Points for consideration:
Whether in the facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal has committed an error while granting compensation?
6. Findings of the Court:
6.1 At the outset, deceased was serving has teacher, which was duly proved by claimants by producing documents and also proved his income by submitting his bank statement and other supporting documentary evidence including acknowledgment letter produced at Exh.40.

One can notice that income which has been reflected in the bank statement of deceased pertains to his salary income, which was variable from month to month ranging from Rs.13,500/- to 12,500/- per month.

It would appear to us that deceased was serving as a NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2999/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined trainer in the DN High School, Anand but it has not come out from any supporting oral evidence substantiated the claim of claimants that deceased was used to receive Rs.15000/-
per month as salary from said institute as her bank statement reflects aforesaid variable income so received by the deceased from her employer.
Be that as it may.

6.2 Keeping every factor in our mind and after going through the documentary evidence so provided by the learned advocate for the original claimant during the course of arguments, we are of the view that the tribunal could have considered monthly income of Rs.13,000/- per month instead of Rs.10,000/- per month as deceased was used to receive Rs.13,000/- per month which is confirmed from his bank statement.
6.3 Thus, in view of the aforesaid, we hold that income of the deceased was Rs.13,000/- per month.

Further, considering the nature of employment, 40% future rise of income requires NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2999/2024 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/12/2024 undefined to be considered as per the dictum of the Honourable Supreme Court in case of Pranay Sethi (supra)
, claimant is also entitled to receive Rs.48,400/- as consortium, Rs.18,150/- towards loss of estate and Rs.18150/- funeral expenses.

6.4 Thus, in view of the aforesaid discussion, observations and findings,
claimants would be entitled to receive compensation as follow;

Monthly income Rs.13000/-
 Prospective Income 40% Rs.5200/-

Total Rs.18200/-
 1/3rd Personal Expenses Rs.6600/-
